data.outcome_summary: This OECD PISA 2022 factsheet summarizes how 15-year-old students in Macao (China) performed in mathematics, reading, and science, and how results changed relative to earlier PISA cycles (notably 2018 and 2012). It reports mean performance trends, proficiency-level attainment (e.g., shares at Level 2 and Level 5/6), and distributional gaps (e.g., widening between top and bottom deciles in mathematics and science from 2018 to 2022). In 2022, Macao (China) shows higher-than-OECD-average performance across all three domains, with 92% reaching at least Level 2 in mathematics (OECD average: 69%) and 29% attaining Level 5/6 in mathematics (OECD average: 9%). The note also highlights within-country equity patterns (socio-economic gradients, gender differences, and immigrant background differences) and contextualizes findings with COVID-related schooling experiences. As a descriptive reporting product, it does not provide an ML modeling pipeline, PV-combining or missing-data procedures, or model-based causal estimates.
